## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the swell period this break needs.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind: SE (135) is the dominant answer: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide (three section pages), and Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages). All are 15 deg from the profile's 120, so they agree. One contradiction: Surf Atlas gives NE offshores (45 deg) and says wind matters less under the cliffs. Swell direction: SW/SSW across eight publishers, and the numeric values (195-205) sit just below the profile optimum of 205-235. Padang Padang Surf Camp gives an exposure window of about 165-280. Tide is still section-dependent. Mid is supported by Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages); The Peak is mid-high (Wikipedia, WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide); Racetracks is low; Outside Corner is low or all tides on big swells. Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf's template field say all tides. Size: working ranges of 3-12 ft (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide's Peak) and 15 ft on big low-tide days (Wikipedia) fit the profile's 3-15. Padang Padang Surf Camp says it holds up to 30 ft, and Wikipedia says Bombie reaches 20 ft (not recorded, a record-style figure). Period: the only numeric value is 14-18 s typical peak-season groundswell (Padang Padang Surf Camp), consistent with the profile's 12 s min and 16 s ideal. Season: April/May-October from five publishers. The peer-reviewed hindcast (J. Marine and Aquatic Sciences, 2018) uses only local wind data, so it describes wind sea (Hs 0.98 m, Ts 5.2 s, from the west), not the groundswell that makes Uluwatu work. Its claims are recorded as not comparable. The excerpts come from its English abstract via Crossref, because ojs.unud.ac.id did not respond. Indonesian Surf Guide and Padang Padang Surf Camp are commercial guide/surf-camp sites (community). Three pages of one publisher (Indonesian Surf Guide) count as one publisher.

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf's template says it starts working under 1 m / 3 ft and its text that The Peak works from 1 ft, the Indonesian Surf Guide that The Peak breaks from waist high, Padang Padang Surf Camp from chest high, and WSL that the 2008 contest ran in waves as small as 2-4 ft; none states a measurement scale.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 4m+ / 12ft and Wikipedia that Bombie and Outside Corner produce 15 ft (4.6 m) waves on big swells, while Padang Padang Surf Camp says up to 30 ft and that it can hold any size; for The Peak, WannaSurf gives 8 ft and the Indonesian Surf Guide double overhead, and WSL's 2008 contest reached 8-12 ft; no source states the scale.
- **Wind · offshore**: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, the Indonesian Surf Guide (three section pages, one publisher) and Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages) name the southeast or the SE trades, while Surf Atlas gives NE offshores.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf's template say all tides and Padang Padang Surf Camp mid, while Wikipedia, WannaSurf's text and the Indonesian Surf Guide give section-dependent tides: mid to high at The Peak (which closes out at low), low for Racetracks and Outside Corner.

## Judgement check

Every field's excerpts were re-read on 2026-10-27. Changes:

- swell_period.ideal: 'typical 14-18 s' -> 'long-period groundswell' (no seconds); the 14-18 s figure is what typically arrives, not a stated ideal.
- swell_direction.acceptable_range: 165-280 deg -> not documented; the excerpt is an unobstructed-ocean sector, moved to swell_direction.exposure.
- swell_direction.ideal_bearing: removed the publisher lists from the value (195-225 deg unchanged; the note names the publishers).
